data.narrative:
KoBold Metals is a Series C climate and energy technology company with a $3.0B post-money valuation and $1B+ in total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws from a peer universe of nine comparable companies across the Climate & Energy sector, including five private companies at similar stages (Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Redwood Materials) and public benchmarks (QuantumScape trading at $3.6B, Enovix at $1.0B).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier from Series C to later-stage rounds, yielding an implied valuation of $5.0B against the $3.0B base. Peer-median methodology examines five same-sector comparables filtered for valuation tier, producing a median implied value of $1.0B with a range spanning $700M (Amogy) to $6.0B (Redwood Materials). The wide peer range reflects heterogeneous technology maturity and commercialization stage within the climate tech space.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $850M to $5.8B, with a median of $3.0B—aligned with the current post-money. This suggests the existing valuation is defensible on median peer metrics, though substantial upside exists under stage-progression logic and material downside under conservative peer comparisons. Key uncertainties include technology commercialization risk and whether public and late-stage private peers fully reflect the capital requirements and regulatory trajectory unique to frontier climate technologies.
